summary: Cleanly re-review fleet and scheduler integrity
objective: Perform a clean independent review of immutable CR-6Q remediated commit c5dcb81cd1167caa4804b5f3c2483d3503b70946 for policy bypass, starvation, capacity races, platform-status drift, stale or future evidence, mixed-identity composition, tenant isolation, and redaction. Produce one source-linked report only. Do not repair code, change contracts, approve the block, merge anything, or rely on the conclusions of CR6Q-REV-001 before completing your own analysis.
semanticAcceptance: Before reading any CR6Q-REV-001 conclusion, the report names the exact reviewed commit and declares that the reviewer profile authored none of the reviewed product commits or the first review; any overlap produces a blocked disposition.

The report independently evaluates policy bypass, starvation, capacity races, platform drift, stale/future evidence, identity and tenant isolation, redaction, default-suite registration, and retained deployment/native gates with source links and concrete failure reasoning.

Every finding has severity, exact file or test evidence, a concrete failure or attack scenario, and one disposition: confirmed, not reproduced, retained gate, or unsupported. Passing tests alone are not treated as proof that no finding exists.
The close recommendation uses exactly accept, changes required, blocked, or reject; it does not approve or merge CR-6Q and does not alter the Codex acceptance matrix.

The report contains no secret, raw host identity, private infrastructure detail, personal path, production artifact, invented observation, code repair, architecture decision, or native/live effect claim.
stopConditions: Stop and leave the jobber unclaimed if Git, Node.js, or repository dependencies are not already available; do not install, download, update, or repair dependencies.
Stop and submit a blocked report if the reviewer profile authored any reviewed product commit or the first independent review, or cannot establish independence.
Stop if the immutable base is unavailable, differs from the capsule, or the review would require changing any path other than the single allowed report.
Stop before repairing code, tests, contracts, migrations, workflow files, or acceptance criteria; report findings for Codex disposition instead.
Stop before any install, download, credential use beyond existing GitHub access, native probe, service, external integration, destructive cleanup, or consequential effect.
